why: Correct and sound for today's app.html: the 25 fixtures hold, and a by-name, by-position or whole read of a column is seen. The rule is an over-approximation. Today 658 whole-read sites exist, most of them plain lookup maps (PHASE_NAME[p], query[army().id], FN_ROW[id]), so every registered column counts as read. Only 35 columns are read by no other form, and none of them is hand (21 derived, 14 sourced). Every hand column is already read by name. The whole rule does not make the check meaningless for hand columns today; it makes it equal to "every registered column is judged". Reviewer fixtures (scratchpad/rvh-tools/smut-rv.js), seen: a generator helper, an object-method helper, an optional computed read u?.[k], D['ruleAliases'], Array.from(row), [re, key] in a named function's parameters. Missed: a top-level `var` helper (START matches only function/const/let, so the body is dropped), Reflect.get(u, k), Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor (singular), aliased or destructured Object.values/entries, and Object.values?.(u). None of these forms is in app.html today, and while any whole read exists they change nothing. Residual: add them to wholeReads and START, with fixtures. Opinion (not blocking): because the rule always fires, it would be more honest either to state it as "every column of verify/columns.json is judged", or to make it precise by tracing. render.js already opens every screen and popup, so it could wrap the data's rows in Proxies (get / ownKeys / has) and record the (table, column) pairs actually read. A whole read is then charged to the table whose row it touches, not to every table. Keep the static by-name scan, unioned with the trace, for safety.

where: review-derived-proof · verify/derived-proof.js; verify/tables.js derivers, keysOf, references; verify/run.js step derived
why: It proves what it says: the named script references the key, and a step that runs that script fails on the changed value where it passes unchanged. In the full gate in a scratch copy, derived passes warm (110 of 131; 21 have no stored value). Reviewer mutations, all refused with NO PROOF: CORE_STRATAGEMS.id relabelled derived by check.js, ARMIES.id by verify/helpers.js, ARMIES.units.short by verify/from-json.js (via catalog), and short by invariants.js + lines.js + waha-words.js (all 17 candidate steps pass on each of the 3 changed values). ARMIES.units.note (gw) relabelled derived by texts.js is skipped as "no value stored in data.js", not failed: a column with no stored value needs only the static reference. The builder's d0-d6 (dmut-out.txt, read, not rerun) are as reported. It can pass for a reason other than derivation in three ways. (1) A crash counts as a proof. ARMIES.units.ds (dangling datasheet id, data.js throws) and BOXES.b.on / st.on / d.on (TypeError in lines.js / defence.js) are proved only by crashes. A reviewer swap to another valid value showed real holders exist: ds to another datasheet fails tables (table form); on to another condition key fails evidence G7. lines.js still crashes on a valid key, though. Suggest: a crash is no proof, and the change is another row's valid value (a swap) rather than " (changed)". (2) A deriver that is a widely required helper (waha-words.js: 17 steps) makes every one of those steps a candidate, so the proof is "some step notices", not "this script derives it"; references() is a weak bar (any x.key or 'key' in the file). (3) The cache key is the step's .js closure only; the JSON and source inputs a step reads (deviations-*.json, derive-agreed.json, verify/sources, .cache) are not in it. A reviewer attempt to exploit this (emptying derive-agreed.json) did not, because derive still fails on its own, but the gap is real when the gate runs warm. Bug (latent, fails safe): change() on a regular-expression token crashes. verify/literal.js regex() reads flags with /[a-z]/.test(src[i]); at the end of the token src[i] is undefined, which tests true as "undefined", so the loop runs until RangeError (seen with FACTIONS.aliases relabelled derived). No derived column holds a regex today. Fix: i < src.length in that loop, or parse the token with text after it. Also safe side: reimport runs from-json.js by spawn, not require, so a column naming from-json.js is not tried against reimport. Cost: about 40 minutes cold, accepted by the coordinator.

why: The label is true. GW's Core Rules PDF 01-06 prints "Your unit must be within range of the selected objective.", and no GW update prints "unengaged". Keep it (the label says plainly where it comes from); whether to show Wahapedia's differing words at all is the owner's call. Reviewer mutation rA, a wcore line with words GW prints ("Each model that is moved must end its move within range of the selected objective if possible, or closer to it if not."), passes. Correct for the label form it reads, "(…, X datasheet)". The Chaos Daemons pack prints each datasheet on two pages (Blue Horrors p52-53, Pink Horrors p54-55, Flamers p56-57; the second page starts WARGEAR OPTIONS). Reviewer mutations: a Pink Horrors label on a Flamers quote fails ("not on the Pink Horrors datasheet … p54-55"); a Blue Horrors label on a Pink Horrors first-page quote fails; positive controls pass (a Flamers label on a Flamers quote; a Pink Horrors label on a quote from its second page, p55). NOTE_LABELS is a closed list in code, so a new label is a reviewed code change; still, match "X datasheet" anywhere in the label.
